alignments.note: ἔσται rendered by the idiomatic *will come*; the auxiliary is a rule 9 helper and the head is the lexical verb.
Postpositive conjunction fronted in English; rule 15 permits the reorder.
Anarthrous Greek noun with a supplied determiner: rule 51's anarthrous clause makes *the* a rule 7 helper on the noun.
Temporal conjunction to *when*.
Article to *the*; rule 19.
Attributive participle rendered by the adjective *sound*.
Noun to noun; split from its article under rule 26.
Ordinary negative to *not*; no negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Inflected verb takes the supplied subject and auxiliary as rule 9 helpers, discontinuously around *not* under rule 15; head on the lexical verb.
Adversative conjunction.
Preposition to *after*; rule 36.
ἴδιος stands attributively between the article and an expressed head noun and carries the supplied possessive, so the article realizes nothing; rule 47's τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν.
*their own* belongs to the possessive adjective under rule 47; head on *own*, the word glossing ἴδιος.
Noun to noun.
Dative reflexive with its case preposition riding along under rule 21.
Auxiliary is a rule 9 helper; head on the lexical verb *heap*.
Noun to noun.
Participle rendered by *having itching*; the auxiliary participle *having* is a rule 9 helper and *itching* carries the κνήθω lexeme.
The ASV writes a bare plural *ears* with no determiner, so the article has nothing to anchor; rule 23.
Singular Greek noun rendered by the English plural; noun to noun.

review_notes: τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας is analysed by rule 47: the article is unrepresented and *their own* belongs to ἰδίας. Giving *their* to the article was the competing reading and is refused because ἴδιος is itself a source word able to take the possessive.
κατά is aligned to *after* under rule 36 rather than being folded into the noun phrase.
